- [USER] User expressed interest in the techniques used to create realistic and detailed creatures in *The Shape of Water*.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The realistic and detailed creatures in *The Shape of Water* were created using a combination of practical effects and digital animation, including intricate prosthetic makeup, CGI, animatronics, and puppetry.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The actors Doug Jones and Javier Botet wore complete body suits, gloves, and facial prosthetics that were hand-painted to look like scales or skin.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Doug Jones's suit weighed around 75 pounds and had a special water-filled layer to simulate underwater movements.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both actors credited their costumes and prosthetics with helping them immerse themselves in their roles.
- [USER] User was surprised by the intricate techniques used to create the creatures and inquired about the difficulty actors faced in performing in those costumes and makeup.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Doug Jones and Javier Botet found it difficult to perform in their costumes due to their intricacy and weight.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Doug Jones had to learn to breathe through a specially designed gill system and express emotions despite heavy facial prosthetics.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Both actors underwent special training and preparation to perform in their costumes, including movement training and enduring hours of makeup application.
